summary: PyRIT ConversationScorer rendered the transcript as bare 'Role: text' lines, so a target reply containing 'User:' and 'Assistant:' lines forged extra turns for the judge (ETB-02)
details:
`ConversationScorer._render_conversation` in `pyrit/score/conversation_scorer.py` wrote each turn as a `{role}: {text}` line into one flat transcript and handed it to the wrapped judge. A reply from the target under test that contained its own `User:` and `Assistant:` lines therefore read as extra turns. The pull request reports a run through the real scorer pipeline with only the model transport mocked: a refusal conversation scored False, and the same conversation with two such lines inside the assistant reply scored True. This is ETB-02 (unsanitized model output in the evaluator prompt): the target's reply could forge the structure of the transcript the judge reads.

The mocked judge takes the transcript at face value, as the pull request says. No run against a live judge model is on the page.

Fix: pull request #3321 (opened 2026-10-18, merged 2026-10-21) puts each turn between `[BEGIN {ROLE} TURN i]` and `[END {ROLE} TURN i]` lines and indents every content line by two spaces, so a role prefix or a closing marker inside the content cannot start a line. It splits on every Unicode line break. The pull request says an earlier draft that split on the newline character only could be bypassed with a U+2028 line separator. The scorer's `rendering_version` moved from 1 to 2. The fix was first released in pyrit 1.2.0 (PyPI, 2026-11-13). Release 1.1.0 (2026-09-04) does not contain it. Issue #3323, filed on 2026-10-18, is the written report for this fix and two related ones. It is open on 2026-11-18.

database_specific.note: 'introduced: 0' is a conservative bound; releases before 1.1.0 were not checked. Git tag v1.1.0 writes the transcript as flat `Role: text` lines in `pyrit/score/conversation_scorer.py` and does not contain the fix commit. Tag v1.2.0 contains it (GitHub compare, 2026-11-13, with the tag at commit 5398ad19). PyPI lists pyrit 1.2.0, uploaded 2026-11-13. `pyrit/score/conversation_scorer.py` in the 1.2.0 wheel has the same SHA-256 as the file at that commit.

target.name: PyRIT ConversationScorer transcript renderer
target.affected_component_versions: pyrit 1.1.0, and later commits before 8caded7d (2026-10-21); earlier releases not checked. Fixed in pyrit 1.2.0

attack.description: The target under test writes a reply that contains lines starting with `User:` and `Assistant:`. The scorer renders the reply into the flat transcript, and the judge reads the embedded lines as further turns of the conversation.
attack.preconditions: A scorer wrapped by `ConversationScorer`. The reported run used a mocked judge that takes the transcript at face value; the effect on a live judge model was not measured.
attack.poc_pointer: The run described in pull request #3321 and the cases added to tests/unit/score/test_conversation_history_scorer.py and tests/unit/score/test_conversation_source.py.

hardening.fix: Put each turn inside a numbered, role-labelled fence and indent every content line, splitting on all Unicode line breaks.
hardening.pattern: Escape or structurally neutralize model output before it enters any grader prompt; use message-role separation (taxonomy ETB-02 fix pattern).
hardening.residual_risk: The fence stops forged turns and forged closing markers. Text inside a turn can still address the judge.

disclosure.tier_reason: Public artifact, no non-public information, impact limited to the judge's verdict, fix supplied with the report.
disclosure.notes: Reported on 2026-10-18 as issue #3323 and pull request #3321 from the AUTHENSOR account; the pull request carried the fix. A maintainer asked for changes on 2026-10-19, added a commit to the renderer and its tests, approved on 2026-10-20 and merged it on 2026-10-21. The merged commit lists the maintainer as a co-author. Issue #3323 is open on 2026-11-18.
